page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration built on the arm64 architecture. Powered by Ampere AmpereOne processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 vCPUs. The hardware platform pairs these processing cores with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per core.

The configuration provides dedicated execution threads that prevent resource contention typically associated with simultaneous multithreading environments. There are no local storage disks bundled with this shape, meaning root volumes and persistent filesystems require attached remote block storage volumes. Accelerators are omitted, with zero GPUs present. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external ingress and egress routing.

In terms of resource architecture and cost efficiency, the AmpereOne arm64 implementation offers predictable execution latency per core alongside power-efficient compute density. The balanced allocation of memory and core resources makes this shape suitable for cloud-native web servers, microservice container hosting, development environments, and general-purpose Linux enterprise workloads optimized for 64-bit ARM architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-16 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores from the Ampere AmpereOne processor family clocked at 3.0 GHz, corresponding to 4 vCPUs with one thread per core. The compute capacity is coupled with 16.0 GB of system RAM, providing an even 4.0 GB per core distribution. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage for operating system images and persistent data, and does not include GPU acceleration. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core scheduling and high power efficiency inherent to the Ampere architecture, this server configuration targets standard general-purpose cloud workloads, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and web applications compiled for ARM64 platforms.
